text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: GPU_CLUSTER_MEMORY_PRESSURE (severity: P1) — affected pool: gpu-prod-1, alert rate: 18/min, trigger: cudaAllocFailed on multiple nodes

pagerduty-bot: Incident 76281 created -> https://pd.example/INC-76281, paging: @sre-oncall, @omar

sre-oncall: ack -> investigating :mag:

omar: I'm taking lead. pinging infra to check node pressure and kvcache evictions.

maria: seeing 502 spikes from hosted API, 20% error for model=redwood-7b-quant on region=us-east-1 in last 3m. linking logs: https://logs.prod/stream/abc

ashwin: I can start draining batch nodes, but that will drop throughput. recommend fallback to small-bert variant for non-critical routes.

omar: run `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --selector=gpu=true` and `kubectl describe pod <pod>` on suspected hosts. also `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.used --format=csv`

ashwin: pasted `nvidia-smi` from node gnode-12:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        MemUtil (%)  Memory-Usage | GPU-Util (%) |
| 0    A100-80GB    96%           77844 MiB / 81920 MiB | 98%        |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

omar: confirmed heavy KV cache retention + a few runaway batch jobs with memory leaks. seeing repeated cudaMalloc retries in logs:
```
E cudaMalloc failed: out of memory at inference_runner.cc:482
E kv_cache: retained_prefix_size=12.3GB
```

maria: customer-impact update: 9 customers with >1% error rate, 2 paying customers on SLA 99.95% showing degraded latencies. CS notified.

sre-oncall: plan: 1) scale up fallback pool (smaller models) via routing policy 2) evict / restart top mem hog pods 3) enable aggressive kv cache eviction for 10m 4) prepare node drain if fragmentation persists

omar: rolling action 1: apply routing override -> switch non-critical routes to redwood-3b-quant. executing now.

ashwin: action 2: `kubectl -n inference delete pod conv-batch-23 conv-batch-27` (force restart) -> pods restarted, monitoring mem usage

ashwin: action 3: pushed runtime flag `--kv-cache-ttl=60s --kv-cache-max-entries=8k` to inference runtime on pool gpu-prod-1.

runtime-lead: also enabling model variant fallback in load balancer: route weight: redwood-7b-quant=30%, redwood-3b-quant=70% for now.

omar: observing immediate drop in cudaAlloc failures. error rate down from 18/min to ~2/min. latency for fallback routes up ~30% but within SLA for non-critical customers.

maria: CS: two impacted customers on enterprise tier, outreach in progress, offering mitigation and ETA.

sre-oncall: escalation: paging infra-lead for persistent fragmentation if OOMs creep back in 20m.

pagerduty-bot: Reminder: if incident not resolved in 15m, auto-escalate to infra-lead.

omar: running a diagnostic script to check slab fragmentation, `nvidia-smi topo --p2p` and collecting dmesg for driver resets.

ashwin: found one pod with runaway cached tensors in a legacy worker, removing its PVC, restarting. results: free memory increased ~9GB on gnode-12.

incident-bot: Metric watch: cudaAlloc failures -> 2 in last 5m, KV cache eviction rate increased x4.

maria: customer update: CS confirmed that mitigation reduced errors, continuing monitoring and will update in 30m.

omar: marking initial mitigation complete. next steps: follow-up RCA, add circuit-breaker for heavy batch jobs, improve autoscaler for fragmentation events, consider kernel/driver tuning.

sre-oncall: handing off to on-call for post-incident monitoring @ashwin for the next 60m.

ashwin: taking handoff. I'll leave routing override for 30m and then start gradual revert if stable.

incident-bot: Incident 76281 -> status: mitigated (P1 -> monitoring). closed? pending postmortem.

omar: thanks team :thumbsup: we should write a short postmortem and add a playbook step for aggressive kv cache TTL on severe memory pressure.

ashwin: noted. I'll draft playbook PR.

runtime-lead: tagging for follow-up: infra + runtime + devex.

incident-bot: thread archived after 7d unless re-opened.
